title: The Khalsa Hears the Offer and Rejects a Lesser Sovereignty

blocks.text: Once Subeg Singh has explained himself, the Khalsa lets him speak and hear out the proposal from Lahore. Money, honors, and political assurances are placed before the gathering, and the Singhs debate whether to reject the offer entirely, take what can help the Panth, or bend the negotiation toward the protection of the weak.

The discussion does not descend into confusion. The Khalsa weighs the proposal collectively, keeps the focus on justice, and receives the material gifts as something to be redistributed rather than privately hoarded by a single claimant.

The decisive issue is rule itself. When the question of title arises, the assembly insists that the Guru has promised true sovereignty to the Khalsa, and that no Mughal rank can replace the destiny already bestowed upon the Panth.
